answer.exemplar: The region is triangular, so the natural order runs x from the y-axis to a sloping edge, and each horizontal slice has a different width. Reversing the order describes the same region as vertical slices, which may give simpler inner limits and make the inner integral easier to evaluate for the planner's spreadsheet.

questions.explanation: Reversing the order describes the same region with a different slicing, and one choice usually gives simpler inner limits. The value of the double integral never changes.

answer.exemplar: Choose a field whose curl is a constant, for instance P = -y/2 and Q = x/2, whose curl is 1 everywhere. Green's theorem then says the boundary integral of P dx plus Q dy equals the double integral of 1 over the region, which is exactly the area of the region.

questions.subject: CALCULUS_II
questions.learningObjective: Explain when reversing the order of integration is useful
questions.stem: A memo asks why reversing the order of integration is a useful technique when evaluating a double integral over a complicated region.

answer.exemplar: Some regions have simple limits in one order and awkward ones in the other, and the choice of order decides which integral is easier to evaluate. Reversing the order also changes the integration to a single antiderivative followed by a second one, which often removes a difficult inner integral while keeping the same final value.

questions.explanation: The order decides which integral is done first, and in one direction the inner integral may be very hard while in the other it is immediate. The value of the double integral is the same either way.
questions.hint: One order often makes the inner integral trivial.

questions.subject: CALCULUS_II
questions.learningObjective: Explain why the planar curl is a single scalar
questions.stem: A memo asks why the curl of a two-dimensional field is a scalar while the curl of a three-dimensional field is a vector.

answer.exemplar: In the plane, the curl reduces to the single quantity Q_x - P_y, because the component perpendicular to the plane does not vary in a planar field, so only one scalar survives. In three dimensions each of the three partial pairs contributes to a different component of the curl vector, and all three are retained.

questions.explanation: Restricting a field to a plane removes the third component and leaves one meaningful pair of partial derivatives. In three dimensions three such pairs survive and are gathered into a vector.

answer.exemplar: The arc length element ds is always positive, so each small piece of the path adds the strength of the field there without any cancellation. answer.exemplar: Green's theorem states that the line integral of P dx plus Q dy around the boundary equals the double integral of the curl over the region.
